text:
Maya: hey team, quick follow-up from tonight's all-hands — can leadership clarify how midyear promotions interact with the standard leveling windows? I heard there are exceptions but not sure when they apply. :wave:
Priya K: great q, thanks for asking Maya. short answer: exceptions exist for mission-critical moves and retention cases, but there's a guardrail process. i'll paste a short summary below. :point_down:
Ethan: is there any whitelist for promo exceptions? asking because two ICs on my team had accelerated work on an urgent feature. :thinking:
Priya K: @Ethan yes — managers can propose exceptions during calibration, but proposals need: 1) manager recommendation, 2) peer/skip-level feedback, 3) leadership sign-off. compensation team evaluates budget impact.
Carlos: timeline question — if an exception is approved mid-cycle, will comp be retroactive to the start of the cycle or effective from approval?
Priya K: depends. typical outcomes:
- approved for retention/critical: comp can be retroactive to start of cycle up to one pay period (case-by-case)
- approved for role-change/level-up: usually effective at approval date
we try to avoid large retroactivity for budget predictability.
Alex: can you drop the short policy snippet you mentioned? quick reference helps managers during 1:1s.
People Ops: shared doc: https://redwood.example.com/hr/promo-exceptions (internal) — includes template for exception requests and checklist.
Priya K: copying the snippet for quick scans:
```
Eligibility: ICs and managers with >6 months in role.
Exception criteria: retention risk, critical technical contribution, org restructure.
Required artifacts: manager rationale, measurable impact, peer feedback, comp rationale.
Decision window: 14 business days from submission.
Retroactivity: up to 1 pay period for retention cases; typically none for lateral/role-change.
```
Maya: thanks — what about leveling appeals after a promo was denied? can someone request re-review quickly or wait until next cycle?
Priya K: appeals are allowed, but we ask managers to submit new evidence or escalation within 30 days. after 30 days it moves to next cycle unless there is new material.
Ethan: for promoted folks who change job family (e.g., IC->EM), does the comp band mapping differ?
Priya K: yes — job-family changes follow the mapped band for the target role. comp team runs a band-sync and confirms market alignment before final approval.
Carlos: any guidance for communicating this to impacted ICs? want to be transparent and not overpromise.
Priya K: recommended script in doc. short version: explain decision, review artifacts considered, offer roadmap/path to next level, and provide clear timeline for revisit.
Alex: will there be a follow-up office hour for managers? a live Q&A would help. :thumbsup:
People Ops: Scheduling a 30-minute manager office hour tomorrow 11am PT — invite coming in #calendar.
Maya: amazing, thanks everyone. i'll share the doc with my leads and prep exception forms if needed. :raised_hands:
Priya K: thanks Maya — open to follow-ups here or at office hour.
People Ops: closing note — retain copies of all feedback in Lattice/HRIS for audit.
Maya: noted.
